newsitem.title: KENYA: RALLYING-MCRAE TAKES CHAMPIONSHIP LEAD WITH SAFARI WIN.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MCRAE TAKES CHAMPIONSHIP LEAD WITH SAFARI WIN.

text.p: Briton Colin McRae won the Safari rally on Monday and jumped to the top of the championship standings.
McRae, driving a Subaru, finished seven minutes and four seconds ahad of fellow-Briton Richard Burns in a Mitsubishi.
McRae was delighted to have secured a hat-trick of victories for his team so far this season and believed his cautious approach proved crucial.
"Nobody would have put me down to be the winner but we have taken it sensibly and reaped the rewards," he said.
"Driving here is nothing like in Europe -- there you go flat-out all the time -- whereas here it is all about going at a speed that isn't going to break the car.
"It's a tough one, not only for me but for the whole team as well. It is a very special win for sure."
McRae had taken the Safari lead at the start of the second day when the first day's overnight leader German Armin Schwarz fell back with a broken suspension.

From then, the 1995 champion dominated proceedings as he set the fastest time on four of the day's five stages despite attempts by spectators to sabotage his challenge by placing a wall of rocks in front of his car on the sixth stage.
That proved to be McRae's only serious difficulty, though he suffered a minor electrical problem on the final day.
Burns's surprise second place meant British drivers finished first and second in a championship rally for the first time.
Kenyan Ian Duncan, in a Toyota, came in third, 11 minutes and 18 seconds behind McRae.
The rally lived up to its reputation as the most demanding event of the season. Just 19 of the original 51 crews were able to start the final day.
Kenneth Eriksson, from Sweden, won the Swedish Rally three weeks ago but did not manage to complete the first stage of the Safari event when he hit a rock midway through the opening 72-km run.

Carlos Sainz of Spain, the world championship leader going into the event, suffered a puncture after swerving to avoid an animal and, although able to continue, got dust caught in his wheel and destroyed the wheel studs.

Reigning world champion Tommi Makinen retired on the second day when a third puncture on the fifth stage forced the Finn to drive with a flat tyre for 40 kilometres. This eventually caused the rear suspension to fail and broke the drive-shaft.

McRae now has 13 points in the drivers' championship after three rounds, with Sainz in second place with 12 and Eriksson and Italian Piero Liatti in joint third place on 10 points. Subaru maintain their lead in the manufacturers' championship.
The next round of the championship is the Portuguese Rally, which takes place from March 23-26.
